title: How many coins stack as tall as the Statue of Unity?
description: The height of the Statue of Unity is changed from metres to millimetres, and each millimetre is one coin. The count is checked by changing the millimetres back to metres.
teaching_notes: One idea: change the height to the unit of the coin, then count one coin for each unit. Watch for students who forget that a metre is one thousand millimetres and stop at one hundred.

source: Find out how many coins should be stacked to match the height of the Statue of Unity. Assume each coin is 1 mm thick.
video_script.why: The child knows that a metre is one thousand millimetres, and now uses that to count how many thin coins make a tall stack.
video_script.substitution: Change the height to millimetres, then divide by the thickness of one coin.
video_script.anchor: a tall stack of coins beside the Statue of Unity, with the height 180 m marked
video_script.payoff_line: Change metres to millimetres, then count one coin for each millimetre
maths_rules: the book takes the Statue of Unity as 180 m tall
each coin is 1 mm thick, so 1,80,000 mm / 1 mm = 1,80,000 coins
video_script.design: One idea: change the height to the unit of the coin, then count one coin for each unit. The statue and the coin stack stay in the anchor band; the working band shows the unit change and the count. No hard clear.
open_questions: The Statue of Unity is 182 metres tall in reality; the book and the worklist use 180 metres, so the video follows 180 metres.

narration: <bookmark mark='m1'/>This is a question from your book.
<bookmark mark='m2'/>The Statue of Unity is about one hundred eighty metres tall.
<bookmark mark='m3'/>Imagine a stack of coins, each one millimetre thick, piled up to that height.
<bookmark mark='m4'/>How many coins would the stack need?

<bookmark mark='m2'/>A stack of coins, each one millimetre thick, is as many millimetres tall as it has coins.

narration: <bookmark mark='m1'/>Given, the statue is one hundred eighty metres tall, and each coin is one millimetre thick.

beats.on_screen: To find: the number of coins in a stack as tall as the statue

marks.m1: the find line is written under the given line

narration: <bookmark mark='m1'/>We have to find how many coins make a stack as tall as the statue.

marks.m1: the heading height in millimetres appears

narration: <bookmark mark='m1'/>Step one, put the height in millimetres.
<bookmark mark='m2'/>One metre is one thousand millimetres, so we multiply by one thousand.
<bookmark mark='m3'/>One hundred eighty times one thousand is one lakh eighty thousand millimetres.

marks.m1: the heading count the coins appears

narration: <bookmark mark='m1'/>Step two, count the coins.
<bookmark mark='m2'/>Divide the height by the thickness of one coin, which is one millimetre.
<bookmark mark='m3'/>One lakh eighty thousand divided by one is one lakh eighty thousand coins.

marks.m3: a tick appears beside 180 m, the height of the statue

narration: <bookmark mark='m1'/>Step three, check by going back to metres.
<bookmark mark='m2'/>One lakh eighty thousand millimetres divided by one thousand is one hundred eighty metres.
<bookmark mark='m3'/>That is the height of the statue, so the stack matches.
<bookmark mark='m1'/>Change metres to millimetres, then count one coin for each millimetre.
<bookmark mark='m2'/>The stack needs one lakh eighty thousand coins.
